AI.motivation: Standard MLLMs struggle with panoramic polar distortion and continuous cylindrical topology, relying on fragmented local views, leading to myopic search and poor error recovery; a global-informed approach with topology-awareness is needed.
AI.method: Global-to-local exploration framework; RoPE Rolling coordinate-shifting positional encoding to model continuous panorama topologies; large-scale EAGLE-360 dataset (14k+ 4K panoramas, 70k+ VQA dialogues); training pipeline combining Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to elicit spatial reasoning and tool-calling.
AI.result: Sets new state-of-the-art for 360° visual search; ~8x accuracy improvement over base model; improved exploration efficiency; demonstrates effective handling of panoramic structure and robust global-to-local reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Validates the efficacy of global priors and topology-aware encoding for panoramic search; provides a scalable dataset and training framework; establishes a strong baseline for 360° visual search tasks and related embodied AI.

title: Combating Textual Noise and Redundancy: Entropy-Aware Dense Visual Token Pruning
summary: Visual token pruning is a crucial strategy for accelerating VLMs by compressing redundant image patches, yet existing methods often fail to preserve critical cues under dense instructions and fine-grained queries. In this paper, we investigate this failure and identify two underlying bottlenecks: the widespread dispersion of textual noise that corrupts dense cross-modal scoring, and the feature fragmentation inherent to standard token selection. To address these issues, we propose Entropy-Aware Dense Pruning (EADP), a framework that reformulates pruning as a structured compression problem. EADP first leverages statistical entropy to quantify and filter out textual noise, yielding a robust, fine-grained instruction relevance score. Subsequently, instead of naive Top-K selection, EADP casts token selection as a submodular maximization problem with a spatial prior, explicitly ensuring a holistic and non-redundant visual representation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EADP improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of VLMs, robustly preserving fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets while achieving SoTA performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Entropy-Aware Dense Pruning (EADP) improves visual token pruning for vision-language models by filtering textual noise via entropy and using submodular, spatially-informed token selection to preserve fine-grained cues under tight budgets, delivering state-of-the-art results.
AI.motivation: Dense instruction-driven VLMs suffer from dispersed textual noise and fragmented visual features during pruning, which degrades performance under strict token budgets.
AI.method: Entropy-based filtering of textual noise to yield a robust instruction relevance score, followed by submodular maximization with a spatial prior for token selection to ensure a holistic, non-redundant visual representation.
AI.result: Empirical results show improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, robust preservation of fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets, and state-of-the-art performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Reframing pruning as structured compression with entropy-aware filtering and submodular selection yields robust and efficient token pruning for dense instructions in VLMs.

title: GeoMix: Descriptor-Free Visual Localization via Global Context and Multi-Detector Training
summary: Descriptor-free visual localization eliminates high-dimensional descriptor storage, preserves scene privacy, and simplifies map maintenance, yet its accuracy still lags far behind descriptor-based pipelines. We identify this gap to insufficient geometric discriminability in geometry-only matching. Without visual appearance, current methods underutilize local geometry cues, lack the global context among keypoints, and overfit to a single keypoint detector. We further observe that descriptor-free matching naturally enables multi-detector training, as heterogeneous keypoints can be optimized in a shared geometry-only space without aligning descriptor spaces. Building on these insights, we propose GeoMix, a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels. Locally, directional and distance-aware embeddings enrich neighborhood aggregation with fine-grained spatial structure. Globally, learnable context nodes aggregate and redistribute scene-wide information via cross-attention to resolve ambiguities beyond local receptive fields. At the training level, Mix-Training exploits this detector-agnostic geometry space to learn representations across multiple keypoint detectors. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night show that GeoMix sets a new state of the art among descriptor-free methods, reducing 75th-percentile rotation error by 89\% and translation error by up to 90\% over the previous best, while generalizing zero-shot to unseen detectors and narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines. Code is available at $\href{https://github.com/YejunZhang/Geomix}{\text{this links}}$.

AI.tldr: GeoMix is a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that enhances geometric discriminability via local directional/distance-aware embeddings, global cross-attention, and detector-agnostic Mix-Training; it achieves state-of-the-art among descriptor-free methods and narrows the gap to descriptor-based pipelines, with strong zero-shot generalization.
AI.motivation: Descriptor-free visual localization trades off accuracy for privacy and simplicity. The gap to descriptor-based pipelines stems from insufficient geometric discriminability: overreliance on single detectors, underutilization of local geometry cues, and lack of global context. Multi-detector training in a geometry-only space offers a path to stronger, detector-agnostic representations.
AI.method: GeoMix strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels: (1) local: directional and distance-aware embeddings enrich neighborhood representations; (2) global: learnable context nodes with cross-attention aggregate and redistribute scene-wide information to resolve ambiguities beyond local receptive fields; (3) training: Mix-Training trains representations across multiple detectors in a detector-agnostic geometry space.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night shows GeoMix achieves state-of-the-art performance among descriptor-free methods, with 75th-percentile rotation error reduced by 89% and translation error reduced by up to 90% compared to the previous best. It exhibits zero-shot generalization to unseen detectors and narrows the performance gap to descriptor-based pipelines.
AI.conclusion: A combination of enhanced local geometry, global context, and detector-agnostic multi-detector training yields substantial gains for descriptor-free 2D-3D matching, suggesting near-parity with descriptor-based methods while preserving privacy and simpler maps.

title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
comment: 15 pages main text, provisionally accepted to ECCV 2026
summary: Models trained via Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) serve as the foundational vision encoders for most modern Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs). Despite their widespread adoption, CLIP models exhibit a critical yet underexplored failure mode: irrelevant text appearing within images confounds visual representations, biasing them toward lexical meaning rather than true visual semantics. This robustness issue, commonly described as a Typographic Attack (TA), exposes a vulnerability that poses a significant risk to safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving. To achieve interpretable and effective robustness against TA, we propose a novel, training-free mechanistic interpretability method. Our method provides sampling-based interpretations of hidden state representations and quantitatively attributes semantic versus lexical focus to individual attention heads. Through probabilistic analysis and circuit mining, we isolate specific Vision Transformer (ViT) components that disproportionately encode lexical information, thereby identifying the mechanistic source of TA. We further show that simple interventions applied directly to the identified circuits, without any additional training, can substantially improve robustness against Typographic Attacks in object classification. These interventions, such as selective adjustment of attention weights, also outperform both supervised and training-free defense methods. Our experiments demonstrate that applying the proposed intervention to the vision encoders of several state-of-the-art LVLMs yields substantial gains in Visual Question Answering accuracy under Typographic Attack interference on RIO-Bench. These results confirm both the efficacy and the generalizability of our mechanistic approach. Code is released at https://github.com/Liu-524/SamplingTAR.

AI.tldr: Training-free mechanistic interpretability identifies and fixes lexical bias circuits in ViT-based CLIP encoders to defend against Typographic Attacks; improves LVLM robustness without retraining, with strong VQA gains on RIO-Bench; code released.
AI.motivation: CLIP encoders leak lexical cues when images contain text, leading to semantically incorrect representations; Typographic Attacks risk safety-critical deployments; need interpretable, training-free defense.
AI.method: Sampling-based interpretation of hidden states; quantify semantic vs lexical focus per attention head; probabilistic circuit mining to locate lexical-information circuits; interventions by adjusting attention weights directly, no additional training; evaluate on LVLMs and VQA under TA on RIO-Bench; provide code.
AI.result: Selective intervention yields substantial robustness gains against Typographic Attacks; outperforms supervised and other training-free defenses; improves VQA accuracy under TA; demonstrated generalizability across multiple state-of-the-art LVLMs.
AI.conclusion: The mechanistic, training-free approach is effective and generalizable for mitigating TA in CLIP-based vision encoders; potential for safer deployment; code released.

title: Seek to Segment: Active Perception for Panoramic Referring Segmentation
summary: Existing referring segmentation models passively process static images captured from fixed perspectives, limiting their applicability in Embodied AI, where agents must perform active perception in the continuous 360$^\circ$ environments. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel task: Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS). In this setting, an agent is required to adjust its viewing direction ($Δθ, Δφ$) to explore the 360$^\circ$ environment, seeking the object specified by a user instruction for segmentation. To tackle this challenging task, we propose PanoSeeker, a memory-augmented agent for efficient APRS. Rather than relying on heuristic scanning, PanoSeeker integrates a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with EgoSphere, an explicit spatial visual memory. By progressively integrating sequential local observations into a unified 360$^\circ$ representation, EgoSphere enables the agent to plan efficient and non-redundant search trajectories. Once the target is found, the agent performs active viewpoint alignment and outputs the segmentation mask. Furthermore, we curate an expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines for Supervised Fine-Tuning, followed by Reinforcement Learning post-training to explicitly optimize PanoSeeker's exploration efficiency. Extensive experiments on our newly established APRS benchmark demonstrate that PanoSeeker achieves superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.

AI.tldr: An active panoramic referring segmentation method (APRS) using a memory-augmented agent, PanoSeeker, that integrates a Vision-Language Model with an explicit spatial memory (EgoSphere) to actively explore 360° scenes for accurate segmentation, plus a supervised+reinforcement learning training pipeline and an expert-search trajectory dataset.
AI.motivation: Static, fixed-view referring segmentation limits Embodied AI. There is a need for agents to perform active perception in 360° environments with memory to avoid redundant exploration while locating and segmenting a target described by language.
AI.method: Introduce APRS task. Propose PanoSeeker that combines a Vision-Language Model with EgoSphere memory to build a unified 360° representation from sequential local observations. The agent plans efficient, non-redundant search trajectories, performs active viewpoint alignment once the target is found, and outputs a segmentation mask. A curated expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines is used for Supervised Fine-Tuning, followed by Reinforcement Learning to optimize exploration efficiency.
AI.result: Experiments on the APRS benchmark show superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: Memory-augmented active perception for 360° embodied vision is effective; the proposed pipeline and dataset establish a new direction for APRS and related tasks.

title: From SRA to Self-Flow: Data Augmentation or Self-Supervision?
summary: Representation alignment has become an effective way to accelerate diffusion transformer training and improve generation quality. Recent self-alignment methods, such as SRA and Self-Flow, further remove the dependency on external pretrained encoders by constructing alignment within the diffusion model itself. However, the mechanism behind the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow, dual-time scheduling, remains under-examined: Self-Flow attributes its gain to interactions between tokens at different noise levels, where cleaner tokens help infer noisier ones. In this work, we revisit this explanation and ask whether the gain instead comes from data augmentation along the noise dimension. To disentangle these factors, we introduce Attention Separation, which preserves the same dual-timestep input as Self-Flow while blocking attention between tokens assigned to different noise levels. Surprisingly, removing such interaction does not degrade performance and can even improve it, suggesting that the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow mainly comes from data augmentation. Furthermore,We show that Attention Separation itself provides an augmentation effect by splitting a single image into multiple effective training parts to expand the training data. Based on these observations, we combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation, and demonstrate the effectiveness of this design on ImageNet.

AI.tldr: Data augmentation along the noise dimension, via Attention Separation, is the main driver of gains from SRA to Self-Flow in diffusion models; cross-noise token interactions are not essential; Attention Separation also acts as augmentation; combining self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and Attention Separation improves ImageNet performance.
AI.motivation: To disentangle the factors behind the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow and identify whether token interactions across noise levels or noise-dimension augmentation drives gains.
AI.method: Introduce Attention Separation to block attention between tokens at different noise levels while preserving the dual-timestep input; evaluate the impact of removing cross-noise attention; demonstrate that Attention Separation acts as data augmentation by partitioning a single image into multiple training parts; combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and Attention Separation, and test on ImageNet.
AI.result: Blocking cross-noise attention does not degrade performance and can even improve it, indicating data augmentation is the primary mechanism; Attention Separation provides an augmentation effect; the combined design with SRA, dual-timestep, and Attention Separation is effective on ImageNet.
AI.conclusion: The improvement from SRA to Self-Flow primarily arises from noise-dimension augmentation rather than inter-token interactions; Attention Separation is a valuable augmentation technique; integrating self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and Attention Separation yields strong diffusion-model performance on ImageNet.

title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
summary: State-of-the-art single-image 3D reconstruction methods often rely on complex hybrid architectures and loss functions, or compress geometry into latent spaces in order to leverage pre-trained latent diffusion models. In this work, we show that such architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary. We introduce a minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer, built on a plain ViT, that operates directly on raw 3D point map patches and is conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3. Unlike existing latent diffusion approaches, we train our diffusion backbone entirely from scratch, eliminating the need for point map tokenizers. Despite its simplicity, our approach surpasses complex latent-based diffusion models while remaining significantly simpler than hybrid alternatives. Notably, it produces sharper geometric structure and is more robust in highly ambiguous regions, such as transparent objects.

AI.tldr: A minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer directly models 3D point map patches with image-conditioned guidance, achieving better results than latent diffusion while being simpler.
AI.motivation: Reduce architectural overhead and complex losses in 3D reconstruction by avoiding latent diffusion and tokenization, using a plain ViT operating in pixel space.
AI.method: Train a diffusion backbone from scratch on raw 3D point map patches; condition on pre-trained DINOv3 image tokens; no point map tokenizers; operate entirely in pixel space using a ViT-based architecture.
AI.result: Outperforms complex latent diffusion models; yields sharper geometry and improved robustness in highly ambiguous regions (e.g., transparency).
AI.conclusion: Minimalist pixel-space diffusion with a ViT on raw point maps is effective for 3D reconstruction and offers simplicity over latent or hybrid methods.

title: Alignment Is All You Need For X-to-4D Generation
summary: Generative diffusion models excel at synthesizing high-quality images, videos, and 3D content under multimodal control. However, arbitrary user-defined modality-to-4D (X-to-4D) generation remains challenging due to the high cost of constructing diverse datasets and the limited scalability of existing methods. This paper presents Align4D, a flexible framework that translates any-modal input into coherent video-3D pairs, using video to guide 4D motion and 3D data to shape 4D geometry. Align4D introduces three key techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment, which searches Video-Aligned and Multiview-Aligned Object Distances (VAOD/MAOD), respectively, to reconcile 4D renderings with video and the priors of multiview diffusion models; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, which constrains known and unknown views through synchronized video and 3D inputs, ensuring consistent 4D generation; and (3) Asynchronous Optimization, which decouples Gaussian attribute and deformation network training to enhance motion and geometry fidelity. We further propose the X4D dataset, which integrates prompt, image, video, and 3D data for benchmarking. Experiments on X4D and Consistent4D demonstrate that Align4D achieves state-of-the-art quality and consistency in X-to-4D generation. Project page: https://miaoqiaowei.github.io/Align4D/.

AI.tldr: Align4D is a flexible X-to-4D framework that translates arbitrary modal inputs into coherent video-3D pairs for high-quality, consistent 4D generation, leveraging VAOD/MAOD, Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, and Asynchronous Optimization; introduces an X4D benchmark; reports SOTA on X4D and Consistent4D.
AI.motivation: X-to-4D generation is challenging due to the need for diverse data and limited scalability of existing methods; arbitrary modality-to-4D generation requires leveraging video and 3D priors to constrain 4D outputs.
AI.method: Three techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment searches Video-Aligned and Multiview-Aligned Object Distances (VAOD/MAOD) to align 4D renderings with video priors and multiview diffusion priors; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment constrains known and unknown views through synchronized video and 3D inputs to ensure consistent 4D generation; (3) Asynchronous Optimization decouples Gaussian attribute learning and deformation network training to enhance motion and geometry fidelity. An X4D dataset is proposed to benchmark X4D generation.
AI.result: Experiments on X4D and Consistent4D show Align4D achieves state-of-the-art quality and consistency in X-to-4D generation.
AI.conclusion: Align4D provides a flexible framework to perform X-to-4D generation by aligning video and 3D priors with 4D outputs, introduces the X4D dataset for benchmarking, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on X4D and Consistent4D.

title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
summary: We present WorldDirector, a highly controllable video world model framework designed for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration. Unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, our framework explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. By leveraging an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera movements and subsequently employing these orchestrated trajectories as control signals for video generation, our approach ensures strict physical logic and appearance stability, successfully preserving the exact visual identities of dynamic entities even when they re-enter the scene after prolonged periods out of view. Experimental results demonstrate that our method supports the synthesis of complex and extended events with unprecedented controllability and persistent dynamic object memory. Project Page: https://worlddirector.github.io/

AI.tldr: WorldDirector is a video world model framework that decouples semantic motion planning from visual generation, using an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera paths and then applying these trajectories as control signals for video synthesis to achieve persistent object memory and stable appearances across long occlusions.
AI.motivation: Existing world models entangle dynamics with rendering and rely on continuous visual observation, which harms long-term identity persistence and hampers controllability for extended events.
AI.method: Decouple motion orchestration from rendering by using an LLM to generate 3D trajectories aligned with camera movements, then use these trajectories as external control signals for video generation, ensuring physical consistency and persistence of object identities even after long occlusions.
AI.result: Demonstrates high controllability and persistence of dynamic objects, enabling synthesis of complex, extended events with stable identities and predictable motion.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling semantic motion from rendering with LLM-guided trajectory control yields strict physical logic, appearance stability, and long-horizon controllability in video world models.
